claims.text: MTP+FEP will reduce the computational cost of TaVCrW melting calculations by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
MTP+FEP will maintain sub-meV/atom accuracy for TaVCrW melting calculations.
The MTP must accurately reproduce the ab initio phase-space distribution, including SRO and electronic-excitation contributions, for FEP to be accurate.
Solid TaVCrW has local chemical SRO corresponding to equilibration near 800 K.
SRO stabilizes solid TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom relative to a random solid solution.
The EAM reference and thermodynamic integration steps will be replaced by a DFT-trained MTP and FEP, respectively.
A supercell containing at least 500 atoms is required to capture the relevant SRO correlations.
The 2000-2400 K temperature range is required to validate the SRO contribution to melting.
Electronic excitations near the Fermi level must be treated explicitly in the GGA-PBE calculations.
MTP can provide near-DFT accuracy at a computational cost suitable for molecular dynamics.
The lower cost of MTP permits extensive sampling of both liquid and solid coexistence configurations.
FEP obtains free-energy differences directly from overlapping phase-space distributions and thereby bypasses the slow convergence of thermodynamic integration.
Training the MTP on diverse configurations allows it to capture the SRO stabilization energy and electronic-excitation-induced melting shifts.
The MTP+FEP free-energy result will differ from TOR-TILD by less than 0.5 meV/atom.
The method will accurately quantify the SRO contribution to the melting-point shift.
TOR-TILD using EAM references and thermodynamic integration requires extensive sampling and has high computational cost.
Including V and Cr configurations at 0 K in the MTP training set will avoid errors associated with GGA-PBE underbinding or overbinding.
Electronic-excitation effects, high-temperature magnetic fluctuations, and GGA-PBE errors for V and Cr may cause additional errors or melting-point shifts not fully represented by the MTP.
The hypothesis is falsified if, on a benchmark such as MoNbTaW at 2000-2400 K, the MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD solid-liquid free-energy differences disagree by more than 0.5 meV/atom.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that electronic-excitation contributions or density-of-states features are captured by the MTP, whereas the uncertainty field says electronic-excitation effects may not be fully captured.
